title: Archive of Custom-made Guides for Orthopedic Surgery
official: Archive of Custom-made Guides for Orthopedic Surgery
summary: The present study aims to design, develop and test an electronic archive to be able to track over time the so-called Patient-Specific Cutting Guides for Orthopedics (in English often known as ' Pa-tient-Specific Cutting Guides'). Surgical Guides (or even more frequently, Patient-Specific-Instrumentation - PSI), i.e., based on medical images of the specific patient undergoing surgery. These are becoming increasingly necessary for complex surgeries, or those requiring careful pre-operative planning, to support both standard and customized metal implants (i.e., those individual-ly made using so-called "3D printing" or "additive manufacturing" techniques, hereinafter referred to as "custom" implants), as well as corrective osteotomies for cases of severe skeletal deformity. From a technical standpoint, it will be necessary to evaluate whether the compilation of the con-trolled-access archive of these surgical guides will be provided and automated by the software tools currently used for their design, or whether the use of an additional standard platform (such as REDCap) will be deemed suitable, or whether the development of an ad-hoc database will be necessary.
criteria:
INCLUSION CRITERIA:

* Patients of both sexes aged 2 years or older
* Patients on the list at the IOR Operating Units for GSM surgery

EXCLUSION CRITERIA:

* Patients under 2 years of age
* Patients who do not require GSM intervention
